To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of cardiac myosin LC II is an excellent marker of the extent of myocardium damaged by acute ischemia.
myocardial infarcts of varying size can be quantitated by serum myosin light-chain levels and that the relationship between infarct and LC II is stronger than that between infarct, CPK-MB, and LDH-1.
the relationship of serum cardiac myosins to myocardial infarcts was studied in dogs and humans, and that cardiac myosins were better than CPK-MB as a marker of myocardial damage.

the development of an assay for the detection of cardiac specific protein in the blood.
the development of a new diagnostic test for acute myocardial infraction.
the clinical and experimental studies on the myocardial infarcts.

serum cardiac LC levels correlate well with infarct sizes and are a useful tool to assess the extent of myocardium involved in the infarction process.
